es.location: Results, Study 3, Opportunity beliefs and Policy preferences
es.quote:
Replicating study 1, participants who read about rising economic inequality rated structural factors as more important (β = 0.266, SE = 0.046,
P
< 0.001, RMSE = 0.815) and individual factors as less important (β = −0.191, SE = 0.039,
P
< 0.001, RMSE = 0.689), compared with participants in the control condition.
Policy preferences.
Regressions also revealed significant treatment effects for both the government and business responsibility items. As depicted in
Fig. 1
, participants in the inequality condition were significantly more inclined to hold both major companies and government responsible for reducing inequality (β = 0.349, SE = 0.095,
P
< 0.001, RMSE = 1.716 for major companies; β = 0.376, SE = 0.098,
P
< 0.001, RMSE = 1.770 for government), compared with participants in the control condition. Similarly, logistic regressions of participants’ views regarding the one group they considered most responsible for reducing inequality (i.e., the forced-choice question) revealed that those in the inequality condition were more likely to select major companies, relative to all other options (log odds β = 0.234, SE = 0.117,
P
= 0.046), or to select government, relative to all other options (log odds β = 0.290, SE = 0.141,
P
= 0.039), compared with those in the control condition.
